pages.title: South Island Giant Moa
pages.text: The $(o)South Island Giant Moa$() ($(o)Dinornis robustus$()) was one of the tallest birds that ever lived. Females could reach their heads over 3.5 metres high and were much larger than males.$(br2)Moa had no wings at all, and their bodies were covered in shaggy, hair-like reddish-brown feathers. They browsed the forests and shrublands of New Zealand.$(br2)They were hunted to extinction within about 200 years of the first human settlement, around 600 years ago.
